title: Scaling back the Digital Humanitarian Network
html:
As the ability for people around the world to help disaster victims was enabled by modern technologies, several new types of groups and organizations began to form. However, many of the formal, traditional organizations were not sure how to access and collaborate with this capacity. So, in 2012, the Digital Humanitarian Network (DHN) was created to raise awareness of these new organizations, provide a ’connecting service’, and develop guidance on how to work together. 

Over the years, several activation requests were supported. But, as both organization types matured, the need for the DHN has diminished (as originally expected). Formal organizations have added information management and digital capacity. New organizations have stabilized and formed lasting partnerships. And, new services have emerged with funding such as the H2H network and FEMA Crowdsourcing.

What does that mean for the DHN? It means that we are stepping and scaling back. No more formal activation processes/teams, no more CMS-based site to maintain (yep, we went static!) and so forth. Our discussion groups (Skype & Google Groups) will remain available. We can still help connect formal humanitarian organizations with the newer digitally-enabled groups. And we will continue to publish occasional papers related to new technologies and trends.

Over the years, several amazing volunteers have been involved in supporting the Digital Humanitarian Network as well as the many partner organizations. I extend my greatest appreciation to each and every one of you.

Our simplified, static website: https://www.digitalhumanitarians.com/

Andrej
